_comment: Reference content shown for each model class. Keys are matched to class_names.json after normalisation (case, underscores and the 'Tomato___' prefix are ignored). category must be one of: disease, pest, healthy.

Bacterial spot.description: Bacterial spot affects tomato leaves, stems and fruit. It spreads in warm, wet weather through rain splash, overhead irrigation and handling of wet plants.
symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves
Spots may develop a yellow halo
Lesions can merge, and affected leaves may drop
actions: Avoid handling plants while the foliage is wet
Water at the base instead of overhead when possible

Early blight.description: Early blight is a fungal disease that produces brown leaf lesions, often with concentric rings. It usually starts on older, lower leaves.
symptoms: Older, lower leaves are affected first
actions: Keep foliage as dry as practical
Mulch to stop soil splashing onto leaves

healthy.description: The model matches this image to the healthy tomato leaf category.
symptoms: No disease pattern recognised by the model
actions: Check leaves regularly for new symptoms

Late blight.description: Late blight is a potentially destructive disease that can spread rapidly in cool, humid conditions and affect leaves, stems and fruit.
symptoms: Pale, fuzzy growth may appear on leaf undersides in humid weather
actions: Inspect surrounding tomato and potato plants
Remove and bag severely affected plants; do not compost them
Seek local agricultural advice if symptoms spread

Leaf Mold.description: Leaf mold is favoured by high humidity, especially in greenhouses and other places with poor airflow.
symptoms: Pale yellow patches on upper leaf surfaces
Olive-grey, velvety mould on leaf undersides
Leaves may curl, wither and drop

Septoria leaf spot.description: Septoria leaf spot produces many small spots, usually starting on older foliage and moving up the plant.
symptoms: Many small circular spots with dark margins
Grey or pale centres, sometimes with tiny black dots
actions: Clear infected plant debris at the end of the season

Spider mites Two-spotted spider mite.description: Two-spotted spider mites are tiny sap-feeding pests that thrive in hot, dry conditions.
actions: Inspect leaf undersides with a magnifier
Follow local integrated pest management advice

Target Spot.description: Target spot causes leaf lesions and can also affect stems and fruit.
symptoms: Brown circular lesions, sometimes with faint rings
Lesions may have a yellow border

Tomato mosaic virus.cause: Tomato mosaic virus (tobamovirus), spread by contact, tools and seed
Tomato mosaic virus.description: Tomato mosaic virus causes mottled foliage and abnormal growth. It is very stable and spreads easily on hands and tools.

Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.cause: Begomovirus, spread by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci
Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.description: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus is a viral disease transmitted by whiteflies. It stunts plants and reduces yield.
symptoms: Upward curling and cupping of leaves
Flower drop and reduced fruit set
actions: Monitor neighbouring plants for similar symptoms
Control whiteflies using locally recommended methods
Seek agricultural advice to confirm the diagnosis
